source.title: Towards Data-Algorithm Dependent Generalization: a Case Study on Overparameterized Linear Regression
source.authors: Jing Xu; Jia-Ye Teng; Yang Yuan; A. Yao

page_placements.theme: Continued fitting and stopping time alter held-out outcomes

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how early stopping and feature covariance relate to generalization in overparameterized linear regression, and reports an early-stopping comparison on noisy MNIST. These results do not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own excess-risk results for early-stopped and min-norm linear-regression solutions across covariance spectra, plus clean-test error for best and final CNN iterates across MNIST label-noise levels. No listed version covers these comparisons. It also cites findings from other work; those are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests early stopping and covariance-dependent generalization, which none of V1–V8 names. Partially corrupted MNIST labels do not establish V1's comparison between fitting fully random labels and generalizing on natural labels. The linear-regression dimension comparisons do not test V2's widening of ReLU networks trained to convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors introduce data-algorithm compatibility and show that trajectory analysis allowing early stopping establishes generalization under weaker covariance conditions than last-iterate analysis in overparameterized linear regression. Their experiments report lower optimal early-stopping excess risk than min-norm risk and lower best-iterate than final-iterate MNIST test error.
record.recipe_differences: The theoretical analysis uses overparameterized linear regression with full-batch GD and constant step size; the additional classifier experiment uses a four-layer CNN with vanilla SGD. The paper studies early stopping and covariance-dependent excess risk rather than the listed interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported linear-regression excess risk varies across covariance spectra. On MNIST, best-versus-final iterate test error is reported at six training-label-noise levels.

fits_no_version.finding: At n=100 and p=1000, optimal early-stopping excess risk is below min-norm excess risk for all six covariance spectra in Table 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In overparameterized linear regression, optimal early stopping can substantially reduce excess risk relative to the limiting min-norm interpolator, with performance depending on feature covariance.

fits_no_version.finding: Best-iterate MNIST test error is below final-iterate error at every reported noise level: 1.07% versus 1.13% without noise, and 2.71% versus 42.95% at 50% noise. No uncertainty estimates are supplied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the reported CNN and SGD recipe on MNIST, the best test-error iterate can outperform the final iterate, especially with corrupted training labels.

record.problems: The MNIST results are reported without uncertainty estimates. The linear-regression excess-risk comparison is based on 1000 independent trials and reports 95% confidence intervals. The empirical CNN experiment is one stated architecture and dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results left out. Figure 1 repeats the 20% MNIST comparison later reported in Table 7; it is not entered as duplicate rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; chance held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as ReLU-network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error, with training to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of learned local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning budgets, and optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equal numbers of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows and should be T6. cannot_determine denotes inability to assess V1–V8, not uncertainty about the transcribed table values. Tables 3–6 add sample-size and feature-dimension comparisons, but these also fit no listed version and do not require version-specific missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training and held-out accuracy comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

relation.reason: The study discusses overparameterization and generalization but its own results address early stopping and data-algorithm compatibility, rather than any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study analyzes covariance-dependent generalization and early stopping in linear regression, with an additional MNIST experiment. Neither tests nor uses a specific V1–V8 finding. Partial label corruption does not establish V1's fully random-label comparison; feature-dimension comparisons do not test V2's network-width claim.

source_check.notes: Table 7 reports best-iterate test errors without uncertainty estimates or a documented independently validated stopping rule. Appendix C.2 and Figure 3 identify the CNN experiments as SGD; the introduction inconsistently describes the 2.88% best iterate as GD.
